what_it_does: When AI engineers try to speed up a slow deep-learning program, existing profiling tools (tools that measure where time is spent) can tell them which low-level GPU programs (called kernels — self-contained programs the GPU executes) took the most time, but cannot connect that back to the high-level Python code the engineer actually wrote. The gap makes it hard to know which line of Python code caused the slow GPU operation. DeepContext inserts a thin 'shim' layer — a transparent interceptor — between the AI framework (like PyTorch or TensorFlow) and the underlying C++ libraries it calls, so every high-level operator call is tagged with its Python-level origin and correlated with the GPU hardware metrics recorded during its execution. Because the shim sits between framework and library, no changes to the framework's own source code are needed, making the tool work across multiple frameworks. An automated analyzer then processes the correlated trace to pinpoint bottlenecks and suggest fixes.
